rows.description: I find a hundred-rupee note in the corridor, and my heart races with ideas of what I could buy. Wanting is natural; a wise choice is handing it to a teacher or asking whose it is.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, compassion, gratitude, honesty, pride
related mind states: anger

rows.description: I think of the child who lost the note and how worried he might be. Imagining someone else's feelings makes returning it feel simple and warm, not like a loss.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, gratitude, honesty, pride, temptation
related mind states: anger, anxiety, empathy

rows.description: Friends say, finders keepers, let's buy chips. I feel torn between fitting in and doing right. I can decline politely, and often a friend quietly feels relieved that someone said it.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: compassion, gratitude, honesty, pride, temptation
related mind states: relief

rows.description: The shopkeeper gives me extra change by mistake. Nobody will know, but I would. Returning it feels awkward for a moment and then makes me feel light and trusted.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, compassion, gratitude, pride, temptation
related mind states: embarrassment, trust

rows.description: My parent hears that I returned a wallet and hugs me. I feel proud, but I should do the right thing even when nobody praises me, because honesty is for me first.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, compassion, gratitude, honesty, temptation
related mind states: affection, pride

rows.description: The child whose money I returned smiles and says thank you. It feels good, but I must not expect a reward each time. Doing right is its own quiet reward.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, compassion, honesty, pride, temptation
related mind states: gratitude

rows.description: At the temple, mosque, church or gurudwara, everyone sings together and I feel part of something bigger. Belonging is precious; I can also ask why we do things, not just copy.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: gratitude, rejection, respect, trust, worship
related mind states: nostalgia

rows.description: My grandmother teaches me a prayer and her eyes shine. I feel loved and rooted. I take it in with respect and can still ask questions later; good elders welcome them.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, gratitude, rejection, respect, trust
related mind states: affection, admiration

rows.description: I listen to the religious teacher's stories and believe them fully. Trust is natural at this age; over time I learn to notice whether teachings promote kindness and never fear, cruelty or secrecy.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, gratitude, rejection, respect, worship
related mind states: fear, trust

rows.description: I thank God for my family and food before eating. The feeling is warm and simple. Gratitude can also become action, like sharing my food with someone who has less.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, rejection, respect, trust, worship
related mind states: gratitude
